Quality Assurance/Control
All data will be analyzed for any relevant information for each experiment. In addition, all data will
be saved for future reference in case any more information is needed for future analysis.
Data and metadata standards
Standards to be used for data and metadata format and content (where existing standards
are absent or deemed inadequate, this should be documented along with any proposed
solutions or remedies).
All data acquired will be linked back to the specific sample tested. The samples are typically
nanoparticles, which will be identified according to the date synthesized. Synthesis conditions and
post-processing will be notated in a lab notebook accordingly.
In addition, metadata may be needed for the instrument conditions used for acquiring. In general,
these will apply for each type of data:

section.description:
Metadata will be stored primarily in the file name of each dataset acquired. Additionally, it may be
notated in the lab notebook used when acquiring.
Policies for access and sharing, and provisions for appropriate protection/privacy
Policies for access and sharing; Provisions for appropriate protection of privacy,
confidentiality, security, intellectual property, or other rights or requirements.
All data will be stored on the research group RAID server, which may be made available in a shared
folder upon request. Depending on the type of data, specific software may be needed to read
propietary file formats. Such details will be explained if requested. There should not be any delay or
embargo periods on the data acquired for this research. If there is, this data management plan will be
updated.
Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution
Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and the production of derivatives.
Permission to re-use or re-distribute data will be granted within reasonable request. The source of the
data must be adequately acknowleged if used, and the appropriate citation should be made if
available.
Plans for archiving and preservation
Plans for archiving data, samples, and other research products, and for preservation of
access to them.
All data will be stored and archived in our research group's RAID server, which already incorporates
data redundancy for backups. It will remain there for at least 5 years after the release of the
corresponding publication or project. All data require for the creation of a research manuscript will
be stored. Additional data acquired will also be stored for future reference in the research group.
Data may be compressed as necessary for data sharing. Metadata files will be stored in appropriate
directories to detail what is being stored in the server.
